🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO THE DEA: PICK A LANE</u>

President Sheinbaum called out Washington's double discourse on security: DEA chief Terry Cole publicly praised Omar García Harfuch as a trusted US ally at the IDEC conference in Buenos Aires — while his agency keeps recycling evidence-free insinuations of cartel "links" to the Mexican state. "They recognize the work of García Harfuch, but then they allude to supposed ties," she said. Mexico coordinates. It doesn't take dictation.

‍US MEDIA SILENCE: Narco-blockades and burnt vehicles across Michoacán after anti-CJNG operation August 19–20, 2026 | 🔴 📰 Burned trucks blocking highways, nine alleged CJNG members arrested in a major security operation, Uruapan and Apatzingán shut down. The story led Mexican coverage and was picked up from Sydney to New Delhi. US mainstream coverage as of Thursday: zero. 🔍 The last time Michoacán made US headlines this month, it was to pause avocado inspections. An actual cartel uprising gets nothing.

‍PUBLIC BOOKS: "Our Guns Make the Violence That People Are Fleeing" August 20, 2026 | 🟢 📰 MacArthur fellow Ieva Jusionyte on Exit Wounds: over 70% of guns recovered at Mexican crime scenes come from the US. Gun stores in US border states: 9,940. In all of Mexico: two. 🔍 The trafficking emergency at the border runs south. A rare US interview that flips the frame: the violence migrants flee is made in America — and it's a business with a lobby behind it. • "It is our guns that make that violence that people are fleeing" • "Now it's sending the guns. And this is where the demand for drugs is"

‍LATIN TIMES: Mexico Faces Pressure to Match Canada's Tariff Relief in Talks With Trump Administration August 20, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Canada just walked out with auto tariffs cut to 15% and steel/aluminum to 25%. Mexico — three rounds of talks, zero retaliation, deeper security cooperation — is still waiting. Mexican industry leaders say Canada's deal "weakened" their government's we're-better-positioned line. 🔍 The omitted number: 85% of Mexican exports still enter the US tariff-free under USMCA — the fight is over the sectoral tariffs Washington refuses to lift. • "Canada's progress has weakened that argument" — Mexican auto and steel industry leaders • Trump on the Canada deal: "very fair"

text: ‍EL PAÍS: Mexico steps up legal offensive over 17 Mexicans who died in ICE custody August 19, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Mexico has filed 20 complaints with US authorities over 17 citizens dead in ICE custody or raids. Four got a response. One Florida prosecutor replied by backing ICE's account of a 19-year-old's death — which detainee testimony and the local medical examiner suggested was a killing by guards. 🇲🇽 Straight report, and it names what US coverage skips: a formal Mexican complaint targets GEO Group, the private contractor running Adelanto, where four of the 17 died. • "There are simply too many cases" — Sheinbaum • "He had forwarded the information to the U.N. Human Rights Council" — Velasco on Volker Türk's reply

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S HEAVY-TRUCK MAKERS TARGET 70% REGIONAL CONTENT BY 2027</u>

Ahead of the fourth bilateral USMCA meeting set for September, Mexico's heavy-vehicle industry is already articulating the jump to 70% regional content value in 2027 — six more points of supply sourced inside North America — while pushing to keep the current rules of origin untouched and to scrap the 25% Section 232 tariff on non-North American content, ANPACT chief Rogelio Arzate told El Economista. Washington debates tariffs; Mexican industry does the homework.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM EXPOSES LA DERECHA DIARIO'S PAID-BOT FAKE NEWS MACHINE</u>

Days after the Bolivia arrest of cofounder Fernando Cerimedo — accused of attempted femicide — President Sheinbaum laid out how the far-right outlet La Derecha Diario actually operates: money in, bots out. "They are not people posting, they are paid robots," she said, recalling that founder Javier Negre "himself published that 'here in Mexico he was contracted by Salinas Pliego'." The right's massive online support was an invoice all along.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO FILES 20 COMPLAINTS OVER 17 MIGRANTS DEAD IN ICE CUSTODY</u>

Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco Álvarez says Mexico is following up on 17 cases of Mexican nationals who died during ICE operations or in ICE custody — and has filed 20 formal complaints with US authorities to establish the circumstances of each death: eight with state prosecutors and twelve with district attorneys in Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Missouri and other states. Not a press release — case-by-case legal pressure, on US soil.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>VERACRUZ AUDITS ALL 260 PUBLIC NOTARIES OVER PROPERTY-THEFT CASES</u>

Governor Rocío Nahle's administration is auditing every one of the 260 notaries public operating in Veracruz, after a string of property-dispossession cases against Veracruz families became public in recent months. Nahle warned she will not tolerate illegal acts that put families' patrimony at risk. Notaries are where despojo gets its paperwork — auditing all 260 is what actually going after land theft looks like.
